full_text:
If you [follow me on social media](https://x.com/DhananiZain), you may have noticed that I am feverishly covering the latest NFL news, applying analytics to the updates, and sharing my takes. Well, now you get a nicely organized, summarized version in article format. __These are the OTA storylines that will help you with your fantasy drafts and that the markets may not be pricing in.__

In this article, I’ll cover my top 10 takeaways from OTAs, plus at least one note for each of the 32 teams.

Top 10 Fantasy Football Takeaways from OTAs
-------------------------------------------

+ __Bhayshul Tuten has a prime opportunity to take over lead back duties in a profitable fantasy football offense.__ He matches the description of what Liam Coen wants to see out of his RBs. Also, Chris Rodriguez had surgery on his foot - which I’ve heard was a [Jones fracture](https://x.com/DrJesseMorse/status/2064188321157284124?s=20). Dez Bryant and Sammy Watkins are examples of players who returned the same season after Jones fracture surgery and posted ~6-7 FPG lower than their previous season’s numbers.

 Big news on Chris Rodriguez: “According to a team source, Jacksonville Jaguars running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. had a procedure on his left foot following an injury earlier in the offseason program, but is expected to be ready for the start of training camp in late July.” https://t.co/AlENPWvLcG — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) June 8, 2026 

+ James Cook is reportedly set to have an increased role in the offense, absorbing at least some of Ty Johnson's pass-catching duties. The Bills brought Pete Carmichael over from the Saints to be their offensive coordinator, and they envision Cook in an Alvin Kamara role. Cook ranked 38th in RB route share last season (min. 5 games), at 37.1%. Alvin Kamara hovered between 49.7% and 60.8% from 2021 to 2023 (when Pete Carmichael was with the Saints, per our charted data). __That would boost his fantasy value from 18 FPG to 20-21 FPG, which is usually a top-3 RB season.__

 James Cook is expected to be more involved in the passing game: This is now 3 different sources and this is a top insider for the Bills If true, huge ceiling elevation for Cook https://t.co/ttNkO38hqK pic.twitter.com/d22q4nlfW5 — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) July 3, 2026 

+ Every news report out of Jaguars OTAs praises how strong a camp Brian Thomas Jr. had, but those reports also describe him as a vertical player, catching deep passes, or some form of the same terminology that defines him as their deep threat. I won’t cover what that means again — [I wrote him up in detail in my last article](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/fantasy-factors-understanding-route-depth#/), but note that __it’s not good to be a deep threat.__

 Brian Thomas, continually mentioned as a deep threat / vertical receiver for the offense Per @FantasyPtsData he had the 2nd highest aDOT in the NFL when Meyers joined the team Deep threats (25%+ Deep Routes) average ~1.8 .5 PPR FPG less than short-tree WRs Article coming soon https://t.co/UXyTE02C4B — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) June 24, 2026 

+ Josh Downs practiced as an outside WR at OTAs and is in line for more opportunities this season. The Colts don’t have many options at this point, with Alec Pierce potentially sidelined with an ankle issue and Ashton Dulin as their WR3. There is speculation that the Colts will add a veteran free-agent WR like Keenan Allen or Deebo Samuel, but it’s also been mentioned that these players would play more of a specialist role (3rd down or obvious passing situations). If Downs earns more than a 75% route share, [__he will smash his ADP and I am betting on it.__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2075419885497131141?s=20)

 Josh Downs expected to play significantly more on the outside in addition to the slot Alec Pierce late July to September Keenan Allen or Deebo Samuel mentioned as potential vet FAs (again) to play in late down situations Ashton Dulin frontrunner for WR3 https://t.co/6aTaENjEKy — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) July 2, 2026 

+ The Texans are considering David Montgomery a three-down back with a role similar to Joe Mixon’s. [Woody Marks will get some 3rd downs](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2067676368821707103?s=20), but I don’t anticipate that being enough to matter. [__The Joe Mixon role__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2073494903930405042?s=20) __was RB10 in 2024 with 17.2 FPG, while David Montgomery comes off the board at RB20.__ If you’re worried about efficiency with Montgomery as he ages, I’m not sure that matters - Joe Mixon had a 4.15 YPC (33rd among RBs with 100 attempts) in his lone season with the Texans.

 On David Montgomery (and Woody Marks): “Montgomery is slated for a heavy workload that includes pass-catching duties as he works in tandem with talented backup Woody Marks. This is a featured role for Montgomery..” Also mentioned Monty as primary replacement for Joe Mixon… https://t.co/rLzCGdcG0B — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) July 4, 2026 

+ Malik Nabers had a secondary surgery to remove scar tissue from his knee, and in his first public appearance, he did not look great. [__No medical professional I’ve spoken to believes he will be near the superstar-caliber player he’s proven to be in the first half of the season (and maybe not at all in 2026).__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2075374395002953867?s=20) This could be a major boost to a player like Isaiah Likely, who figured to be a top-2 target earner on the team anyway (typically fantasy gold for TEs).

 It’s a charity event video so take it with a grain of salt but it does not look like Malik Nabers has a normal gait yet when he’s jogging here https://t.co/mZnISkb7wz — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) May 31, 2026 

+ By all accounts, including from George Kittle himself, __he is ahead of schedule and should be ready by Week 1__ ([though he may not play Week 1 due to travel](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2066524742740238745?s=20), so he’s much more likely to play Week 2). You can read why he’s a great bet at cost [here](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/brain-trust-favorite-best-ball-pick).

 More George Kittle positivity - 3 for 3 on DPTs / MDs having similar opinions Ahead of schedule and Week 1 looks possible New procedures + advanced rehab + meds = historically fast recoveries https://t.co/Gfym8vg7Xu — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) June 25, 2026 

+ Jahmyr Gibbs finally has his own backfield — we no longer have to worry about David Montgomery at the goal line. Being a bellcow is huge for Gibbs, who has consistently overperformed his XFP. He finished as RB2 and RB3 in 2024 and 2025, respectively, but was RB17 and RB6 in Team XFP Share (Bijan Robinson was RB4 and RB3). __He is the clear 1.01 for 2026.__

 Clear RB pecking order for Lions: Jahmyr Gibbs (bellcow) Isiah Pacheco (spell back, clear RB2) Sione Vaki (RB3) https://t.co/fFw7cMPsjb — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) June 10, 2026 

+ Rome Odunze had a stress fracture in his foot at the end of 2025, tried to play through it (ineffectively), and now has to deal with the “new normal” feeling in his foot. Medical professionals believe this could have a [significant impact on Rome’s outlook](https://x.com/jmthrivept/status/2063283981127418305?s=20). On the flip side, Ben Johnson is “[buying Luther Burden stock](https://x.com/kfishbain/status/2060040702755553637?s=20).” Ben Johnson is not known for praising his players publicly. I view [Luther Burden’s deployment as similar to Amon-Ra St. Brown’s](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2055320609748299941?s=20), __so I too am buying Luther Burden stock.__

 Underrated comment from Rome Odunze who has permanent foot damage that could alter his play for the rest of his career 👇 "This is my new normal. And it’s not from a standpoint that I’m always in pain but the way my foot broke there’s callouses in there that create a different… https://t.co/TIFOydDcUU — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) June 3, 2026 

+ Kenneth Walker hasn’t come close to a featured role in his career, and now he gets to play in a favorable offensive environment. We just saw what a bellcow role for Walker looks like when he posted 24.9 FPG over three games in the 2025 playoffs with Zach Charbonnet sidelined. __If he gets a bellcow role, he has the skill set to put up 20 FPG (usually a top-5 RB), and he goes off the board as RB9.__

 On Kenneth Walker role: "Chiefs are hoping Walker's impact is similar to what happened when Saquon Barkley joined the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024.. Chiefs have never had a feature back capable of carrying the offense at times. The Chiefs signed Walker to be that player." https://t.co/qCZ0sUHGcD — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) June 9, 2026 

The Most Important Note for All 32 Teams
----------------------------------------

\> __NOTE:__ Ryan Heath addressed schematic changes in his latest ground-breaking article, with a lot of news from this piece, [here](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/).

### Arizona Cardinals

+ [Carson Beck will likely be the starter by the time the fantasy playoffs roll around.](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2070916408767123895?s=20) If you exclude Brock Purdy, the average stat line for 3rd-round (or later) QBs that started 3+ games as a rookie is as follows (since 2021):

Pass YPG: 196.7

Pass TD/G: 1.00

INT/G: 0.77

Rush YPG: 12.6

Rush TD/G: 0.07

FPG: 12.0

+ __The above impact is very significant for Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr., and Michael Wilson; it will cap the upside for all three.__

### Atlanta Falcons

+ Kyle Pitts will be a focal point in the offense and will not be just a deep threat — [the team is expected to play a ton of 12-personnel under Kevin Stefanski](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2066571490879782927?s=20) (see Ryan Heath’s playcaller article), which means __the days of limiting Kyle Pitts’ route participation are done.__

### Baltimore Ravens

+ [__Rashod Bateman is WR2 for now__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2072916498201407896?s=20) as the team evaluates veteran WR options. There is a WR3 competition between Devontez Walker (current favorite), Elijah Sarratt, and Ja’Kobi Lane. Sarratt stood out the most in this group during OTAs, but it is too early to know their roles.

### Buffalo Bills

+ There is a WR3 competition among Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer, and Skyler Bell, which could also result in a gross split that makes none of them fantasy-viable. __Skyler Bell is the most interesting of these options__ since we’ve never seen him and he was impressive in OTAs.

### Carolina Panthers

+ [__Jalen Coker is the clear WR2__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2067233078351655048?s=20) and received a large contract extension, while [Xavier Legette is expected to battle rookie Chris Brazzell in training camp for WR3 duties.](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2065075263923212600?s=20)

### Chicago Bears

+ D’Andre Swift is still [viewed as the lead back](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2073906904590352486?s=20), with Kyle Monangai as the bruising RB2. The backfield projects to be a similar split to what we saw in Week 13 and beyond in 2025, when Swift was RB11 and Kyle Monangai was RB35 (min. 3 games). Swift and Monangai go at RB21 and RB34, respectively, so __the price is cheap for Swift and fair for Monangai.__

### Cincinnati Bengals

+ Ryan Heath covered this a bit [here](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/), but the [Bengals practiced more under-center play-action](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2069960503690952811?s=20) (UCPA) to open up explosives in both the passing and running games. They feel that Erick All is a key to doing this because he poses a legitimate threat as a blocker and pass catcher. __UCPA is a fantasy cheat code we want our players to be involved in__, and the Bengals rank near the bottom of it annually. Hopefully this is wheels up for Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins.

### Cleveland Browns

+ [The star of OTAs was Denzel Boston](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2070252845719544107?s=20), who lined up primarily as an outside WR in the spring. It’s hard to tease out whether personnel led Todd Monken to a higher percentage of 2 or fewer WRs on the field in Baltimore or whether he prefers heavier sets, but __if he does go with 2 WRs, it sounds like Boston would be on the field.__

### Dallas Cowboys

+ George Pickens showed up to [mandatory minicamp](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2072729695725011367?s=20) after signing the franchise tag. There is no expectation of a holdout. Meanwhile, the team is considering [__using him more in the slot.__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2075099914548162641?s=20)

### Denver Broncos

+ The backfield resembles the [split](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2068189239221580161?s=20) the team exhibited early in the 2025 season: JK Dobbins is the lead rusher, RJ Harvey factors in as a spell back with pass-catching duties, and Jonah Coleman spells Dobbins a few times and handles pass-protection work. This backfield is a mess for redraft; __if I had to pick one for best ball, it’s JK Dobbins__ since he will have games where he scores 15 or more points, like he did three times in 2025.

### Detroit Lions

+ Sam LaPorta is expected to be back healthy for training camp.

### Green Bay Packers

+ Christian Watson and Matthew Golden figure to be the WRs in 2WR sets, and Jayden [Reed is still primarily a slot receiver](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2074501698366664795?s=20).

### Houston Texans

+ [The Texans want to do more 12 personnel](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2064453956147818854?s=20) (2TE, 2WR, 1RB) in 2026. Their TE room was decimated by injuries in 2025. Now they have brought in Foster Moreau and Marlin Klein (a 2nd-round rookie) along with a healthy Brevin Jordan and Cade Stover. This matters because all reports point to [__Jayden Higgins being the WR2 for the team with Jaylin Noel operating as the team’s primary slot__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2064206399035334730?s=20) (who may not play as often).

### Indianapolis Colts

+ Jonathan Taylor has a history of right ankle injuries (though he stayed healthy last season), so __the RB2 battle between DJ Giddens and Seth McGowan (or a veteran free agent the team could sign) is one to watch.__ [Both rotated with the first team](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2062359124751298616?s=20) (Giddens went first).

### Jacksonville Jaguars

+ [Travis Hunter is going to primarily focus on defense and be a part-time WR this season](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2075007429851431395?s=20). If he runs 40% of the routes, the other three WRs (Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr., and Parker Washington) could each reach 70%+ route share. A 70% route share would rank WR56 (min. 5 games), but we have precedent for players like Tyreek Hill, Jaylen Waddle, and Puka Nacua putting up big seasons with those shares. Those are elite names, however, so if this Travis Hunter route share is true, it would be concerning for the rest of the receiver room. __I am fading the idea that the percentage is consistently that high and think it’s more plausible he plays the 18-30% route-share role that Tim Patrick ran last season.__

### Kansas City Chiefs

+ [Patrick Mahomes is on track to do 11-on-11 work in training camp](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2071577467966378144?s=20) and should be cleared for Week 1 if everything goes smoothly.

### Los Angeles Chargers

+ [The Chargers want to get the ball out within 2.5 seconds and have a YAC-heavy approach](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2065893813172736210?s=20). This is a stronger stylistic fit with Quentin Johnston’s skill set coming out of college. Previously, Johnston was cast in a deep-threat role, so __this would be a major change, making him much more intriguing.__ [Scott Barrett also compared Quentin Johnston to Deebo Samuel](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2069800473037549816?s=20).

### Los Angeles Rams

+ [Terrance Ferguson, who plays TE, is expected to operate as the de facto WR3 and take on a larger role in the offense](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2070140865599697162?s=20). This is similar to the Tutu Atwell role, which does not lead to many targets because it is a deep-threat role, but __we like taking darts on players who are on the field in a potent offense in the last few rounds of drafts.__ [There is not really a great comparison for Ferguson (when he did run routes) last year — he truly just ran deep](https://x.com/HaydenWinks/status/2064357508299604378?s=20).

### Las Vegas Raiders

+ [__Tre Tucker__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2062926046391923002?s=20) __and Jalen Nailor are expected to be the team's top 2 WRs.__ The Raiders are not expected to sign a veteran free agent WR at this time. [Jack Bech and Dont’e Thornton are competing for WR3 duties, but the team will be in 2WR sets more often this season.](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2071943522739978474?s=20)

### Miami Dolphins

+ [Greg Dulcich was Malik Willis’ favorite target at OTAs](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2067719294272549118?s=20), and he’s been considered a team and locker room leader for the Dolphins. He should almost assuredly be a top-2 target earner in this offense. __You could take worse late-round chances than Greg Dulcich.__

### Minnesota Vikings

+ [A Vikings insider believes that Jordan Mason is the lead and early-down back for the Vikings, while Aaron Jones is mainly serving in a spelling role and contributing on passing downs](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2073499081092034977?s=20). That is different than what I initially thought. __The masses faded Javonte Williams in 2025, so you can tell yourself a story of how Jordan Mason gets there.__

### New England Patriots

+ Newly acquired WRs AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs are both likely to be full-route-share players, with the [rest of the WR room rotating around them](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2066955200640745492?s=20). __There’s no reason to draft anyone in this WR room other than these two at this point.__

### New Orleans Saints

+ Jordyn Tyson and Chris Olave both missed OTAs; however, Olave is now cleared from his blood clots and is practicing with Tyler Shough in California. We still have not seen Jordyn Tyson, which is cause for concern given his injury history. Regardless, the expectation is that [Jordyn Tyson operates as the short and intermediate target, while Chris Olave works as the deeper target](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2066955200640745492?s=20). __If Jordyn Tyson is healthy, he’s my number one rookie WR to target in this up-tempo Saints offense.__

### New York Giants

+ Cam Skattebo returned to practice at OTAs and did a backflip at a charity softball event. [__There’s no cause for concern about his availability for Week 1 at this time__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2072354748506788190?s=20).

### New York Jets

+ Adonai Mitchell and Geno Smith displayed [strong chemistry](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2067967033312956748?s=20) at OTAs. Mitchell has notoriously been a strong separator but struggles with drops and mental mistakes. He seems to have a full-time role for the Jets, similar to his role down the stretch last season — __taking a flier in the late rounds isn’t the worst idea for someone who could be “this year’s Alec Pierce.”__

### Philadelphia Eagles

+ One of the concerns coming out of college was Makai Lemon being more of a slot-only player, and so far he’s mainly been featured in the slot in his limited reps at OTAs. He also sustained a hamstring injury, but is expected to be fine for training camp. __I’m on record saying that he’s a bad fit for how Jalen Hurts operates__ — [he does not like to target the middle of the field](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2049927457361330332?s=20) — which is where I expect Lemon to thrive. He’s also less likely to play in 2WR sets, further limiting his opportunities. There’s significant variance in how Sean Mannion may operate his scheme and how many 3-plus WR sets we may see (the Packers, where Mannion comes from, were at 68% in 2025), and there’s no certainty that Lemon will play in 2WR sets.

### Pittsburgh Steelers

+ [__Rico Dowdle is expected to be the early-down back, with Jaylen Warren as the pass-protection and pass-catching back__](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2074969814154486232?s=20). There’s potential for some overlap as well, but this seems pretty clear based on multiple reports.

### Seattle Seahawks

+ [George Holani and Jadarian Price were splitting first-team reps at OTAs, with Holani getting the first look](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2064916520241680434?s=20). This could easily be Olabisi Johnson over Justin Jefferson all over again… or it could be Chris Carson over Rashaad Penny. This is one to monitor in training camp. __Regardless of the outcome, neither would likely become a bellcow, given the offensive philosophy and Jadarian Price’s limited receiving history.__ Zach Charbonnet is also ahead of schedule and figures to add to this mess by the fantasy playoffs.

### San Francisco 49ers

+ The coveted Christian McCaffrey handcuff role is a [50/50 training camp battle between Kaelon Black and Jordan James](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2064503801222926820?s=20). __Stay close to this one — this figures to be a high-scoring offense, and we want the handcuff given McCaffrey’s extensive injury history, touches, and age.__

### Tampa Bay Buccaneers

+ The coaching staff is envisioning a 1A/1B rushing attack with Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell. Kenneth Gainwell would also get pass-catching duties. Bucky practiced in the spring, so that is a good sign for his availability, but by all reports the team wants to limit his touches given his frame and injuries. [The team also feels like they want to ride the hot hand at RB](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2070698727774339195?s=20), which I’d argue could be Kenneth Gainwell depending on which version of Bucky Irving we get (2024 vs 2025). __I am targeting Kenneth Gainwell at the moment.__

### Tennessee Titans

+ There are questions at multiple starting offensive line spots, with the unit coming in at [27th in Fantasy Points Offensive Line Rankings](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-offensive-line-rankings#/). The poor line play could lead to more short passes, which fit Wan’Dale Robinson’s profile better than Carnell Tate’s, even though Tate could be an elite talent (Brett Whitefield compared him to CeeDee Lamb). I also question whether Brian Daboll is actually a QB whisperer and whether Cam Ward will be a quality QB. __I don’t love the overall environment, and that has me leaning away from Carnell Tate.__

### Washington Commanders

+ By all accounts, [the Commanders are either deploying a WR-by-Committee at WR2 or they sign a meaningful veteran WR to slot in at WR2](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2068678900889113066?s=20). After the recent Brandon Aiyuk feud with Jayden Daniels, __my bet is that Stefon Diggs is the Commanders’ target__ (the only other veteran free agent mentioned by reporters). Diggs is already a smash at ADP, and his value will rise wherever he signs, but this could be a nice landing spot. I’m not very interested in any of the other prospective WR2s on the team.
author: Zain Dhanani
